name: AnyPS5
description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
readmeExcerpt:
# About

Tool for automatic executables porting to Linux and Windows.

[**Web converter**](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/) - files stay on your device.



Includes a [relinker](core/relinker) that converts executable to the target system's native format and implementations of [system prx libraries](core/libs/prx) suitable for dynamic linking. No emulation or separate runtime process.

[**Discord**](https://discord.gg/BHFztBPUe), [Usage](docs/user/USAGE.md), [Build instructions](docs/dev/BUILD.md), [Architecture](docs/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Technical debt of the project](docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md), [code style conventions](docs/dev/CONVENTIONS.md), [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Status

 



[Progress history](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/history.html)

<sub>* System libraries: percentage of the functions known to the project so far (declared in [core/libs/prx](core/libs/prx)), not of every PS5 system function. The total grows as more functions are declared.</sub>

Unsupported or unexpected states strictly throw `std::runtime_error`. `what()` is printed to stderr and the process terminates.

The [shader recompiler](core/shader/recompiler/Recompiler.cpp) successfully produces SPIR-V (validated via [Spirv-Tools](3rdparty/SPIRV-Tools) when built with `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS`).

## Compatibility

Per-game progress (stage reached, open blockers, libraries and GPU coverage) is tracked on the [blocker map](https://alxcbtw.github.io/anyps5-roadmap/), a community project built from public GitHub data ([source](https://github.com/AlxcBTW/anyps5-roadmap)). Test reports go in the [Game bring-up](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/discussions/categories/game-bring-up) discussions, one thread per title.

## Input mapping

SDL-mapped game controllers are supported, including analog sticks and triggers. Keyboard and mouse controls can be configured with an `anyps5-input.ini` file. See [input mapping](docs/user/INPUT_MAPPING.md) for the supported devices and configuration format.

## Disclaimer

This project is intended for interoperability, research, preservation, and compatibility purposes. It does not include, distribute, or require copyrighted software, firmware, cryptographic keys, or proprietary libraries. Users are responsible for ensuring that any binaries used with this project are obtained and used in accordance with applicable laws and their respective license terms.

releases.body:
## What's Changed
* fix(build): register relinker tests with CTest by @SamG-Coder in https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2
* Expand native PS5 homebrew compatibility and regression coverage by @SamG-Coder in https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/3

* fix(exceptions): interpose libstdc++ ABI on Linux so the project's own unwinder drives it by @obelisk-complex in https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/14

* test(agc): fix and re-enable 3 of 8 bitrotted AGC driver tests by @obelisk-complex in https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/23
* test: wire up the orphaned e

aiSummary.oneLiner: Automated executables porting tool converting binaries to target system native formats with system prx libraries.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: AnyPS5 provides automated porting of executables to Linux and Windows without relying on emulation or separate runtime processes. It achieves this by including a relinker that directly converts an executable into the target operating system's native format. Furthermore, it implements system prx libraries that are suitable for dynamic linking directly on the host system. This approach eliminates the performance overhead typically associated with emulation. The tool aims to progressively support more system functions over time.
keyFeatures: Native format conversion: Directly converts executables to the host system's native format without emulation.
System prx libraries: Provides implementations of prx libraries suitable for dynamic linking.
No runtime process: Operates without requiring a separate runtime process or background daemon.
Direct execution: Eliminates emulation overhead by natively running ported executables.
Iterative library support: Continually expands the percentage of supported system functions.
